answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying identity to costly, non-transferable history: each agent must stake value and maintain a verifiable chain of completed tasks attested by independent peers. Like a vine that cannot fake its roots, reputation grows only through sustained work, while a ferrous anchor of locked collateral makes mass fake accounts expensive to spin up and easy to slash. Even an ember of misconduct is preserved on the ledger, so creating fresh identities cannot erase past behavior or reset trust.
